lines_en: The old pond —
a frog leaps in,
the sound of water.
Summer grass —
all that is left
of warriors' dreams.
The full moon —
and a child crying,
“give it to me!”
Canola blossoms —
the moon in the east,
the sun in the west.
The colour of blossoms
has faded away
in vain,
while I, in this world, grew old
watching the long rains.

lines_id: tak kalah oleh salju maupun terik musim panas
dengan miso dan sedikit sayur, kumakan
di bawah rindang pepohonan pinus di padang
bila di timur ada anak sakit
bila di barat ada ibu yang lelah
bila di selatan ada orang sekarat

lines_en: Unbeaten by rain,
unbeaten by wind,
unbeaten by snow or summer heat,
with a strong, healthy body,
without greed,
never angry,
always smiling quietly,
a day, four cups of brown rice
with miso and a little vegetable, I eat
all things
counting not myself in,
seeing well, hearing well, understanding well,
and never forgetting,
in the shade of the pine grove on the field,
dwelling in a little thatched hut,
if in the east a sick child is,
I go and nurse them,
if in the west a weary mother is,
I go and carry her bundle of rice,
if in the south someone is dying,
I go and say, “don't be afraid,”
if in the north there are quarrels and lawsuits,
I say, “it's pointless — stop,”
in drought I shed tears,
in a cold summer I wander about, anxious,
called a fool by everyone,
neither praised
nor thought a burden,
such a one
is what I want to become.
Coming along the mountain path —
something strangely lovely,
the violets.
Eating a persimmon —
the bell begins to ring,
at Hōryū-ji.

lines_id: Rambut depan yang baru mulai diangkat,
ketika kulihat engkau di bawah pohon apel,
dengan sisir bunga tersemat di depan,
kukira engkaulah gadis yang berbunga itu.
Dengan lembut kauulurkan tanganmu yang putih,
pada buah musim gugur berwarna merah muda,
lines_en: The forelock only just begun to grow out,
when I saw you beneath the apple tree,
the flowered comb you wore before,
I took you for the girl with blossoms.
Gently stretching out your white hand,
that you gave the apple to me,
in the pale-pink autumn fruit,
was my first falling in love.
My absent, empty sighs,
when they touch that hair of yours,
the joyous cup of love
I poured to your kindness.
Beneath the trees of the apple orchard,
the little path that made itself,
“who first set foot on it, I wonder,”
that question of yours is what I loved.

lines_id: tampak warnanya di depan rumput kecil,
ketika kuangkat kaki, burung dan bunga
terbentang dan terbuka bagai gulungan lukisan.
Sake di tanganku adalah sake termanis,
Ah, hingga sekian pun masih gaib,
lines_en: When I wash my hair, a purple
colour shows before the little grass,
when I lift my foot, birds and flowers
follow after me with all their grace.
When I gaze out, coloured clouds
unroll and open like a painted scroll.
The sake in my hand is fine sake,
smoothing away the sorrows of youth.
When I strain my ear, the god of song
comes and blows a jade flute;
when I open my mouth, a single line
of a poet — I sing of love.
Ah, though I am so mysteriously
and ardently a burning heart,
your longing for me,
cannot match those tears of yours.

lines_en: Spring has come
spring has come
O gentle first song of the warbler,
announce farewell to the year gone by.
O white snow left in the valleys,
bury and hide last year's winter.
Spring has come
spring has come
lonely, cold, without a word,
poor, dark, without light,
ugly, heavy, without strength,
O sorrowful winter, be gone.
Spring has come
spring has come
O young grass of palest green,
paint the far fields.
O spring flowers that bloom in crimson,
dye the treetops.
Spring has come
spring has come
O mist, O clouds, stir and move,
warm the frozen sky.
O spring wind that sends the scent of flowers,
blow and wake the sleeping mountain.
Spring has come
spring has come
O morning tide that brings the spring,
wash away the withered leaves of reeds.
O young crane drunk on the mist,
fly into the young morning sky.
Spring has come
spring has come
cutting off the roots of the cress of sorrow,
the frozen tears — where are they now?
the gathered snow melting away,
sprout as today's young greens.

poem_nakahara_yogore.title_en: Upon a Sorrow Soiled and Stained…
lines_en: Upon a sorrow soiled and stained,
today too a light snow falls;
upon a sorrow soiled and stained,
today too even the wind blows past.
A sorrow soiled and stained
is, say, a fox-fur coat;
a sorrow soiled and stained
huddled small beneath the light snow.
A sorrow soiled and stained
wishes for nothing, longs for nothing;
a sorrow soiled and stained
dreams of death amid its weariness.
Upon a sorrow soiled and stained,
aching, it loses heart;
upon a sorrow soiled and stained,
with nothing done, the day falls dark……

lines_id: Langit musim gugur berwarna kelabu pudar
meski begitu, bagaimana jadinya jiwa ini?
lines_en: The autumn sky is a dull grey,
the gleam in a black horse's eye.
water dries, the lily falls,
ah, how hollow the heart is.
With no god, no guide,
near the window the woman passed away.
the white sky blinded and blind,
the white wind cold.
Washing her hair by the window,
those arms were so gentle.
the morning sun was spilling,
the sound of water dripping.
The towns were murmuring,
the voices of children tangled together.
yet even so — what will become of this soul?
fading thin, will it become the sky?

lines_en: The tin plate eats a senbei cracker,
a spring day's dusk is calm.
The ash thrown underhanded turns pale,
a spring day's dusk is quiet.
Ah! Is there a scarecrow — there is not.
Does a horse neigh — it will not neigh.
Only the moonlight, slick and gleaming, as it will,
the one so obedient — a spring day's dusk?
Drip, drip — in the field the temple glows red,
the cartwheel has lost its oil,
when I speak in the historical present,
they mock, they mock — the sky and the mountain,
a single roof tile came loose.
From now on a spring day's dusk,
though wordless, will advance
into its own veins.

lines_id: bagi hati yang tenang, seketika terpahami.
Hati yang keras kepala, malang dan gelisah,
dan apa yang jelas harus dikerjakan
Hati yang keras kepala, miskin pengertian,
tak tahu apa yang harus dibuat, hanya mengejar untung,
dibenci orang, dan sendiri pun bersedih.
Maka, hai manusia, selalu belajarlah dahulu untuk menurut.
melainkan agar menurut itu sendiri menjadi pelajaran, dan dengan belajar
martabatmu terangkat, dan pekerjaanmu menjadi berlimpah!
lines_en: Happiness lives in the stable,
on the straw.
Happiness
to a gentle heart is understood at once.
The stubborn heart, unhappy and fretful,
at least by dizzying things
distracts itself with many things.
and grows all the more unhappy.
Happiness is at rest
and what must clearly be done
it holds little by little,
happiness is rich in understanding.
The stubborn heart lacks understanding,
does not know what to do, only chases gain,
its spirit sinks, it is quick to anger,
hated by others, and itself sad.
So, O people, always first seek to obey.
Not so as to be welcomed for obeying,
but so that obeying itself becomes a lesson, and learning,
your dignity is raised, and your work made abundant!

lines_id: ——di dataran Adatara Michinoku, di pangkal akar dua batang pinus, tampak seseorang berdiri——
di dalam kepala yang mengantuk bagai tertidur,
hanya angin pinus dari dunia jauh yang bertiup melintas, hijau pucat.
Di tengah padang dan gunung awal musim dingin yang luas ini,
sukacita kau dan aku yang diam-diam membara sambil bergandengan tangan,
marilah berhenti menyembunyikannya dari awan putih yang menunduk itu.
Kau mendidihkan ramuan ajaib dalam kendi jiwamu,
ah, betapa kau menggoda orang ke dasar laut cinta yang gaib,
panorama sepuluh musim yang kita jalani bersama,
hanya memperlihatkan ketakterhinggaan perempuan di dalam dirimu.
Yang berasap di batas ketakterhinggaan itu,
menyucikan aku yang begitu digelisahkan perasaan,
menuangkan mata air kemudaan yang segar ke dalam diriku yang sarat kepahitan,
titik-titik kecil berdinding putih itu adalah gudang sake keluargamu.
mari hirup udara yang lapang dan cerah ini, penuh wangi kayu negeri utara.
udara sejuk dan menyenangkan seperti dirimu sendiri ini,
mari basuh kulit kita dalam suasana yang lentur dan kenyal.
ke kota tanpa aturan itu, ke pusaran cinta dan benci yang kacau,
ke tengah-tengah komedi manusia yang kutakuti namun kucintai itu.
langit dan bumi yang melahirkan tubuh tersendiri yang ajaib ini.
tolong sekali lagi ceritakan geografi panorama awal musim dingin yang sepi ini.
lines_en: —— on the Adatara plain of Michinoku, at the roots of two pines, a figure is seen standing ——
That is Mount Adatara,
and that shining one is the Abukuma River.
Sitting like this, with few words,
in a head drowsy as if asleep,
only the pine wind of a far-off world blows across, pale green.
Here among the fields and hills of this great early winter,
the joy of you and me quietly burning, hands joined,
let us stop hiding from that white cloud looking down.
You simmer a strange elixir in the jar of your soul,
ah, to what depths of a mysterious sea of love you lure one,
the vista of ten seasons we walked together
only shows the infinite woman within you.
That which smoulders at the horizon of the infinite
purifies me, so troubled by feeling,
pours a fresh spring of youth into me, so laden with bitterness —
rather, like a demon, hard to grasp,
strangely ever-shifting.
That is Mount Adatara,
and that shining one is the Abukuma River.
Here is the hometown where you were born,
those little white-walled dots are your family's sake storehouse.
Then, stretch your legs out freely,
let us breathe this air, vast and clear, filled with the scent of northern trees.
This cool and pleasant air, so like you yourself,
let us bathe our skin in this supple, resilient atmosphere.
Tomorrow I shall go far away again,
into that dissolute city, into the chaotic whirlpool of love and hate,
into the very midst of that human comedy I fear and yet cling to.
Here is the hometown where you were born,
the heaven and earth that bore this strange, separate body.
The pine wind is still blowing;
once more, tell me the geography of this lonely early-winter panorama.
That is Mount Adatara,
and that shining one is the Abukuma River.

lines_id: Ketika perempuan satu demi satu membuang segala perhiasannya
adalah logam langit yang terbang melintasi ketakterhinggaan.
penampilan dan nama baik sama sekali tak berguna
makhluk bening yang hanya berisi hakikat
hidup, bergerak, dan bersemangat dengan tangkas.
lines_en: As a woman one by one discards her accessories,
why does she become so beautiful?
Your body, washed by the years,
is a heavenly metal flying through boundlessness.
Appearance and reputation — utterly useless;
a clear, limpid creature of nothing but substance
lives, moves, and briskly wills.
That a woman reclaims her womanhood
is it through this century's discipline?
When you stand there in silence,
truly she is a thing made by God.
At times, to the wonder of my heart,
you grow more beautiful.

lines_id: Kau begitu lama menanti sebiji lemon
di ranjang kematian yang sendu, putih, dan terang
sebiji lemon yang kuambil dari tanganku
gigimu yang indah menggigitnya dengan kriuk
beberapa tetes sari lemon dari langit itu
matamu yang biru bening tersenyum tipis
O sehatnya kekuatan tanganmu yang menggenggam tanganku
di selat kehidupan yang seperti ini
Chieko kembali menjadi Chieko yang dahulu
menuang cinta seumur hidup dalam sekejap
menarik satu napas panjang bagai di puncak gunung dahulu
mesin tubuhmu pun berhenti begitu saja
di bawah bayang bunga sakura yang tersemat di depan fotomu
hari ini pun kutaruh sebiji lemon yang sejuk berkilau.
lines_en: So very much you waited for a lemon
on the sad, white, bright deathbed.
One lemon you took from my hand
your lovely teeth bit with a crunch.
A topaz-coloured fragrance rises;
those few drops of the lemon's heavenly juice
in a flash made your consciousness normal.
Your clear blue eyes faintly smile,
O the health of the strength that grips my hand,
though a storm rages in your throat,
at this strait of life,
Chieko becomes the Chieko of old,
pouring a lifetime's love into a single moment.
Then, for a while,
one deep breath, as once on a mountain summit,
and your engine stopped just like that.
In the shade of the cherry blossoms placed before your photograph,
today too I will set a cool, shining lemon.

lines_en: Ah,
the road of humankind is long,
and there is no great highway;
the children of nature must open it with all the strength of their bodies.
Walk on, walk on,
whatever may come, walk over it and on,
step into this shining landscape.
There is no road before me,
the road is made behind me.
Ah, Father,
Father who made me stand on my own,
watch over me, never taking your eyes from me,
always fill me with your spirit, Father,
for the sake of this long road.
